title: EduCare Connect - pilot study institutions
summary:
Every year, around 2,250 children and adolescents in Germany are diagnosed with cancer. Due to the intensive treatment they receive, many of them are unable to attend regular school classes for long periods of time. This not only leads to learning deficits, but also to a loss of contact with classmates and teachers, which can be accompanied by loneliness and psychological stress. Avatars offer a possible solution here: they are placed in the classroom and enable the affected children to participate in lessons from home or from the hospital and maintain contact with their class. Initial studies suggest that this form of participation can promote mental well-being, social integration, and learning. However, there has been little research on this topic in Germany to date.
In the pilot study of the EduCare Connect research project (former projekt title: Avatar4School), employees of institutions (e.g., support associations, clinics, schools) that provide the avatars are asked via an online questionnaire about the conditions and procedures for giving an avatar to children and adolescents with cancer. In addition, individual interviews are conducted with experts from these institutions to learn more about the current state of avatar use.
conditions: Conditions and procedures for the use of avatars with children with cancer

interventions.name: Employees of institutions (support associations, clinics, educational institutions) that provide avatars to children and adolescents with cancer.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Employment: Position at an institution that provides avatars to children and adolescents with cancer
• Language skills: Native-level proficiency in German
• Technical requirements: Stable internet access
Exclusion criteria:
No experience in providing and supporting the use of avatars for children and adolescents with cancer
